focus: Settling in: getting to know the room, routines and each other. Daily listening and oral-blending games (Phase 1 aspects) — no letters yet.

days.objective: Build listening and speaking-sound skills through "Listening Walk" — settling in, no letters yet.

phase1_aspect.name: Listening Walk
phase1_aspect.description: Helps children notice and name the everyday sounds around them, indoors and out, as the very first step towards careful listening.

games.title: Sound Hunt Basket
games.how_to_play: Take a small basket on a walk around the garden or a nearby street, stopping every few steps to listen. Each time you hear something — a car, a bird, a gate creaking — pop a matching picture card or small object into the basket. Back inside, tip out the basket and see who can remember what made each sound.

games.title: Freeze and Point
games.how_to_play: Play outdoors or on a walk. Every time the adult rings a small bell, children freeze on the spot and silently point towards where the last sound they heard came from, then whisper what it was.

days.keep_up: Same-day boost: any child finding a game hard gets it again in a smaller group with more adult support.

days.objective: Build listening and speaking-sound skills through "Instrument Sounds" — settling in, no letters yet.

phase1_aspect.name: Instrument Sounds
phase1_aspect.description: Introduces children to sounds made with real and homemade instruments, building their ability to hear differences in pitch, volume and pattern.

games.title: Instrument Corner Guess
games.how_to_play: Sit children in a circle with a screen or blanket hiding a small set of instruments — drum, bells, shaker, tambourine. Play one out of sight and children guess which instrument it was, then reveal it and pass it round the circle.

games.title: Loud and Quiet March
games.how_to_play: Give every child a homemade shaker, such as a bottle with rice inside. March around the room together, playing loud when the adult holds up a big sun picture and quiet when a small cloud picture is held up.

days.keep_up: Same-day boost: any child finding a game hard gets it again in a smaller group with more adult support.

days.objective: Build listening and speaking-sound skills through "Body Percussion" — settling in, no letters yet.

phase1_aspect.name: Body Percussion
phase1_aspect.description: Gets children making rhythmic sounds with nothing but their own bodies, so they always have an instrument close to hand.

games.title: Body Sound Orchestra
games.how_to_play: Stand in a circle and go round naming a body sound in turn — clap, stamp, click, pat knees. Once everyone has chosen a sound, the adult 'conducts' by pointing to different children to build up a whole-group rhythm.

games.title: Echo Me
games.how_to_play: The adult claps or stamps a short pattern, such as clap-clap-stamp, and children echo it back exactly. Patterns get a little longer and trickier as the game continues.

days.keep_up: Same-day boost: any child finding a game hard gets it again in a smaller group with more adult support.

days.objective: Build listening and speaking-sound skills through "Rhythm & Rhyme" — settling in, no letters yet.

phase1_aspect.name: Rhythm & Rhyme
phase1_aspect.description: Fills the day with nursery rhymes, songs and rhyming words so children start to feel a steady beat and hear when words chime together.

games.title: Rhyme Basket Match
games.how_to_play: Fill a basket with pairs of small objects or picture cards that rhyme, such as cat and hat, star and car. Children pull two out at a time, say them aloud, and decide whether they rhyme, sorting them into a 'yes' pile and a 'no' pile.

games.title: Beat the Bongo
games.how_to_play: Sing a familiar nursery rhyme together while children pat the steady beat on their knees or a small drum. Every few lines, pause and have the group clap the beat alone before the singing continues.

days.keep_up: Same-day boost: any child finding a game hard gets it again in a smaller group with more adult support.

days.objective: Review week: revisit favourite listening games from the week, including "Alliteration" — still no letters, just checking who is confident joining in.

phase1_aspect.name: Alliteration
phase1_aspect.description: Tunes children's ears in to words that start with the same sound, an early step towards hearing the individual sounds inside words.

games.title: Silly Soup
games.how_to_play: The adult pretends to stir a big pretend cooking pot and invites children to add a silly ingredient that starts with today's chosen sound, for example 'I'm putting in a banana, a ball and a bear!'. The sillier the better.

games.title: Matching Sound Table
games.how_to_play: Lay out a mix of small toys and objects on a table, where several share the same starting sound. Children sort them into groups by their starting sound, saying each object's name aloud as they go.

days.keep_up: Same-day boost: any child finding a game hard gets it again in a smaller group with more adult support.
